text.p: Libya featured for the second time this week as a quoted end-destination on the sugar freight market to import European bagged sugar, shipbrokers said on Tuesday.
Anderson Hughes issued an account order for 14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Dunkirk to Libya for 24/28 February, they said. Details of the actual chartering party are as yet unclear.
On Monday Shyvers Savoy issued an account order for 14,000 tonnes of sugar, again in bags, from Antwerp to Libya for 28 February/4 March.
Market sources said the two inquiries suggested that Libya might have finally filled some of its requirement from last month's buying tender.
Libya tendered about a month ago to buy two cargoes of white sugar for shipment in February/March.

Elsewhere, Pakistan is thought to have bought at least 10 cargoes of Thai sugar over the past few weeks, including two cargoes ordered last week, with Cargill, Kerry and E D & F Man among the sellers.
The vessel Yan Men, chartered by Cargill, was scheduled to leave a Thai port around February 14 to Pakistan with 12,000 tonnes of white sugar, shipping sources said.
Activity at Thai ports is still dominated by white sugar loading for Indonesia. At least 286,830 tonnes had been, or would be, delivered to the country between February and early March, they added.
Glencore entered the market with an inquiry for 13,500/14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Thailand to Indonesia for February 23/March 5.
Kerry's recent orders for Thai sugar into south Korea, China and Indonesia were still open, they added.
In other news, Syria tendered to buy 13,000 tonnes of white sugar and 13,000 tonnes of raws, with the two amounts to be shipped in April. The final date for receiving offers was set for February 26.
The Cyprus-flagged freighter Nika II ran aground in gale force nine winds at Veracruz anchorage, Mexico, Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service said on Tuesday.
The 15,251 dwt vessel was awaiting berthing instructions when strong winds caused it to drift and run aground.
It sailed from Abidjan on January 23 and was inbound to Veracruz to load a cargo of bagged sugar for Algeria.
